summary: Kansas is among the most permissive states for the roof rat. The Dangerous Regulated Animals Act (K.S.A. 32-1301+) covers only big cats, bears, and non-native venomous snakes — no rodents. KDWP's exotic-wildlife rule (K.A.R. 115-20-3) AFFIRMATIVELY allows possessing, breeding, and selling non-native species with no permit (just confine them and never release). The Pet Animal Act covers rodents but exempts a resident home breeder who sells only animals raised on their own premises, and its dealer license targets dog/cat sellers. So keeping, breeding, and selling/giving a captive-bred roof rat is legal; the only open edge is whether an import CVI applies (pocket pets are exempt from the import permit; confirm the CVI with the Dept of Agriculture).

keep.why: The Dangerous Regulated Animals Act (K.S.A. 32-1301/-1302) lists only big cats, bears, and non-native venomous snakes — no rodents. KDWP's exotic-wildlife rule (K.A.R. 115-20-3) permits possession of non-native species (confined, not released) with NO permit. KDWP's nuisance-control guidance states no permit is required for Norway rats or house mice. No statute restricts keeping a captive-bred roof rat.

breed.why: K.A.R. 115-20-3 permits possession/breeding of non-native species without a permit. The Pet Animal Act (K.S.A. 47-1701+) covers rodents but EXEMPTS a resident home breeder who sells only animals produced and raised on their own premises — so hobby breeding needs no license.

sell_give.why: K.A.R. 115-20-3 expressly authorizes sale of exotic (non-native) wildlife with no KDWP permit. The Pet Animal Act's pet-shop license is needed for retail of animals NOT raised on your premises; a resident home breeder selling their own is exempt, and the 'animal distributor' license targets dog/cat dealers. Free adoption is unregulated.

transport.why: K.A.R. 115-20-3 requires confinement but doesn't restrict intrastate movement. For IMPORT, the Dept of Agriculture exempts 'pocket pets' (rats/hamsters/gerbils/mice) from the zoo/exotic-animal import permit; whether the general 30-day CVI rule applies to pet rodents isn't explicit — confirm with the KDA Import Desk. Never release (K.A.R. 115-20-3 no-release).
transport.governing_law: K.A.R. 115-20-3 (confinement/no-release); KDA Division of Animal Health import rules (pocket pets exempt from permit).

restrictions.summary: K.A.R. 115-20-3 requires exotic wildlife to be confined and never released into Kansas lands/waters. Importing? Pocket pets are exempt from the KDA import permit; confirm any CVI with the Import Desk. Check local ordinances.
